a:r.a:t: Glycolysis and Gluconeogenesis Are Differentially Regulated by F-2,6-bP

p:cNvPr.descr: The first graph on the left has a vertical axis identified as PFK-1 activity (% of Vmax), and has markers at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100. The horizontal axis is identified as fructose 6-phosphate (mM) and has markers at 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.7, 1.0, 2.0, and 4.0. The graph has a dashed black line going horizontal at 50 on the PFK-1 axis and goes across to 2.0 on the fructose 6-phosphate axis, then goes straight down to 0 vertically. There is also another vertical dashed line at 0.075 beginning at 0 on the PFK-1 axis and goes up to 50. A solid red line, identified as plus F26BP, starts at 40/0.05 and goes up and to the right to about 90/0.7 and then levels off horizontally. A solid blue line, representing minus F26BP, begins at .1/0.05 and goes strictly horizontal to .1/0.7 before it starts curving up vertically to 100/4.0.

p:cNvPr.descr: On the right graph, the vertical axis is identified as FBPase-1 activity (% of Vmax) with markers at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100, and the horizontal axis is identified as fructose 1,6-biphosphate (micro M) with markers at 0, 50, and 100. A dashed line begins at 50/0 and goes horizontally to 50/90, then goes down vertically to 0/90. A dashed line also goes from 0/0 to 50/0. A solid red line, representing plus F26BP, gradually moves up and to the right to approximately 55/120. A solid blue line, representing -F26BP, begins at 0/0 and goes almost completely vertical up to 100/25, the dips right slightly to approximately 80/120.
